sections.heading: Not Sure You Need a New System? Here Is What One Customer Saw
body: A replacement quote is the biggest number an HVAC company hands a homeowner, so it's fair to want another set of eyes before you say yes. Someone has to look at the system to know whether it needs a repair or a replacement.

One customer describes a second look that "got to the possible root of my problem" before they bought a furnace. If you were quoted a replacement elsewhere, call and tell us what the system is doing. If the answer is new equipment, the estimate is free and the work is quoted up front.

sections.heading: Furnaces, Air Conditioners, Heat Pumps and the Rest
body: We install, repair and maintain the equipment that heats and cools a Fort Wayne house. Here is what that covers, and what to watch for with each.

items.title: Furnaces and boilers
items.text: A furnace that cycles on and off, blows cool air or won't light needs a look before the cold weather settles in. We install, repair and maintain furnaces and boilers.

items.title: Air conditioners
items.text: If the house won't cool, the air from the vents is warm or the unit is noisy, turn it down and call. Tell us what it's doing when you call.

items.title: Heat pumps
items.text: One system heats in winter and cools in summer, so it works hard all year. We install, repair and maintain heat pumps.

items.title: Mini splits
items.text: No ducts, one unit on the wall. A mini split suits an addition, a sunroom or a room the ductwork never reached.

items.title: Unit heaters
items.text: Garages, shops and warehouses often heat with a hanging unit instead of a furnace. We install, repair and maintain unit heaters for commercial and industrial spaces.

sections.quote: Absolutely wonderful service. Had an emergency call on a Friday afternoon and they had a service tech at our door within 30 minutes.

sections.heading: Everything We Install, Repair and Maintain
sections.intro: One phone number covers the furnace, the air conditioner, the heat pump and the mini split, in homes and in light commercial buildings.

sections.heading: Started in the Trade in 2005, Then Service Manager at JF Miller
body: I started in the HVAC trade in 2005 as a high school junior. Then I spent 12 years with JF Miller here in the area as Service Manager.
I've kept up continuing education since. JD Kuhn is locally owned.

sections.quote: I’ve used them before and they are always professional and efficient. My tenant complained of the AC not working at all in their apartment. It turns out a new capacitor was needed. The service tech, Chris Wakeland, was in and out in an hour to hour and a half.
sections.name: Kristina B.

sections.heading: For Landlords and Light Commercial Owners
body: If you own a rental, the call comes from you but the cold or the heat is someone else's problem. A tenant without air in July doesn't wait politely, and you can't be there to let anyone in.

We write yearly service agreements for residential and light commercial systems, and we install, repair and maintain unit heaters for commercial and industrial buildings. Call from wherever you are and tell us what's going on.

sections.heading: The Yearly Service Agreement
body: The yearly service agreement is for residential and light commercial systems. It includes two annual services, discounts on consumables and parts, and 24-hour emergency service.

Filters are sold with or without a service visit, so a clean one is easy to keep in the system. Ask about the agreement when you call, and we'll go through what it includes before you sign up for anything.

sections.quote: Eric at JD Kuhn does a great job getting our HVAC System ready to go in the spring and fall. The owner Justin is also great to deal with and very knowledgeable in his field. Highly recommended.
sections.name: Chris V.

sections.heading: Add-Ons, Tight Spaces and the Odd Job
body: Not every job is a straight swap. A cabana, a sunroom or a finished basement can need its own heating and cooling. Mini splits are made for that.
Ask us what's missing from the system you have now, whether that's central air or a filter.

sections.quote: Justin and the guys always do an excellent job. They installed a mini split in our new Cabana. The finished product was very clean and neat. They are always prompt and their follow up is great.
sections.name: Mike P.

sections.heading: Weekdays, 8 to 4:30, and Kristen in the Office
body: Our hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and we're closed Saturday and Sunday. Customers mention Kristen in the office, who they say is friendly when they call to make an appointment.
Geothermal, duct cleaning, gas inserts and fireplaces aren't what we do. When one of those comes up, we send you to a local business that does, so you don't wait on us for nothing.

items.a: No, and we'd rather say so than guess. We refer those to local businesses that do them.

sections.heading: A Free Estimate, and the Number Before the Work
body: Estimates for equipment replacement are free at JD Kuhn. All work is quoted up front, which means the price is on the table before a crew touches anything.

A free estimate is also a fair way to compare. Get ours, get anyone else's, and put them side by side. Look at what equipment is named, what labor is included and what the total is. A number you can compare is a number you can trust.

image.alt: Close view of a new furnace cabinet and ductwork

sections.heading: Repair or Replace: Four Signs You're Past Repairing
body: Most systems don't fail all at once, and a repair is often the right call. Here's how to tell when it isn't.

items.title: The repairs keep coming
items.text: One repair on an old system is normal. A second and a third in the same season usually mean the whole machine is wearing out, not one part.

items.title: A major part has failed
items.text: A cracked heat exchanger on a furnace or a failed compressor on an air conditioner is a major repair on top of old equipment. That's when new starts to make sense.

items.title: It can't keep up with the house
items.text: Rooms that never get comfortable, or a system that runs all day, can mean worn-out equipment or equipment that was never the right size.

items.title: It's very old
items.text: If your furnace or air conditioner is decades old, ask what replacing it would involve before the next repair.

tail: If you're not sure which side of that line you're on, that's what the free estimate is for.

sections.quote: Awesome people, the whole crew did an above the level job, replacing a 70 year old furnace and installing a first time central air unit in this house, we are so pleased with JD Kuhn, recommend them to anybody, thanks again guys.

sections.heading: Before You Say Yes to Anyone's Quote
body: Whoever you call, ask the same four things. What exactly is wrong with the system now? Could a repair fix it? What equipment is being quoted, and what's included in the price? Who does the work?
A company that answers all four plainly is one worth hiring. We expect to be asked, and we'd rather answer them on the phone than at the door.

sections.quote: We had a new AC unit installed. They have become our go to for heating and AC needs. I love the communication with text messages.

sections.heading: Furnace, Air Conditioner or Both at Once
body: Some homes need only one. Others have a furnace and an air conditioner of the same age that are both nearing the end. Replacing both at once can make it one project instead of two.
Heat pumps, boilers and mini splits are replaced and installed here too. If you're adding central air to a house that never had it, say so on the first call, because the ductwork changes the job.

sections.quote: JD Kuhn installed a new air conditioner and furnace this past summer for me. … Even though the repair was a little more challenging than anticipated, Eric stuck with the project and did a great job!

sections.heading: Filters, Tight Spaces and What Rides Along With a New System
body: A new furnace is a good time to ask what else belongs with the system. Filters are sold with or without a service.
Tight spaces are a fact of old houses. If your furnace sits in a closet, a crawlspace or a corner of the basement, tell us when you call, so the estimate fits the space.

sections.quote: Very professional! They were able to install 4 inch filter rack and whole house humidifier in a very tight space. I would highly recommend for any HVAC needed!

sections.heading: After the Install, a Yearly Service Agreement Keeps It Running
body: New equipment still needs a check. The yearly service agreement covers residential and light commercial systems with two services a year, discounts on consumables and parts, and 24-hour emergency service.
A furnace and an air conditioner that get looked at twice a year are less likely to surprise you in January or July. Ask about it when we quote the system.

sections.heading: Replacement Questions Worth Asking

items.q: Is the replacement estimate really free?
items.a: Yes. Estimates for equipment replacement are free.
All work is quoted up front, so you'll know the total before work begins.

items.q: Can you replace just the furnace, or just the air conditioner?
items.a: Yes. We install both heating and air conditioning, together or one at a time.

items.q: Do you install heat pumps and mini splits?
items.a: Yes. Heat pumps and mini splits are on our list of installation, repair and maintenance work.

items.q: What if I'm not sure I need a new system at all?
items.a: Call anyway. Tell us what's happening, and we'll tell you what we think it needs. Sometimes the answer is a repair.

why: Your site is one long page, and on a phone it runs 768 pixels wide on a 390 pixel screen, so a visitor scrolls sideways to read it. Most HVAC searches happen on a phone. There's no contact form either: Book Now opens a Housecall Pro window, and in our test that window showed nothing after three seconds.
Your customers already describe the shop you are. Faye P. wrote "Kristen in the office is so nice and a pleasure to work with." Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo opens with HVAC company in Fort Wayne, IN, leads with a straight second look before a big replacement bill, and gives HVAC replacement its own page.

offer.heading: The offer we'd build with you
offer.text: This is a proposal for you to decide on, not something JD Kuhn does today. It's a second-opinion visit for anyone holding another company's replacement quote, with the visit price texted before anyone is booked and the repair and the replacement written side by side. As far as we found, none of the Fort Wayne companies we checked offers it.

You text back the price of the visit before anyone is booked.
A tech finds what actually failed, and you write down the repair and the replacement side by side. Terms and price are yours to set.
